SMTO-API-0013 — API internal failure

GUID: 5fbf735c-1900-440d-bf2e-317525893cba
Slug: api-internal-failure
Domain: API · Subsystem: api

What happened

  • Something went wrong inside SMTO or a Gateway (the helper program that runs commands for SMTO). Your action may or may not have finished. This message does not tell us what caused the problem.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check whether your action already happened: reload the page and look for its result, such as the saved change, the new message, or the command's output in the task. The failure may have happened after the work was done, and repeating it could do it twice.
  2. Only if you're sure it didn't happen, try the action once more. If you can't tell, ask the person who manages SMTO to check first. This message does not establish whether your action finished, so one new attempt is safe only after you know it made no change.
  3. Select Copy error details and send them, with the time it happened, to the person who manages SMTO. The error reference lets them find the matching entry in the SMTO or Gateway logs.

What success looks like

  • You know whether the original action finished, and the feature works again.

If it still fails

  • There is no confirmed quick fix for this error. Don't keep repeating an action that changes things, and don't delete data or change settings to try to fix it; leave that to the person investigating.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An SMTO or Gateway route hit an unhandled internal exception (for example 'Gateway agent execution failed.' on /exec or a streaming command) or returned an otherwise unclassified HTTP 500.

What this means

  • A Gateway route catches an internal exception, or HTTP enrichment cannot resolve a more specific registered error/status and falls back to the internal API category. Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.

Why this can happen

  • A Gateway route catches an internal exception, or HTTP enrichment cannot resolve a more specific registered error/status and falls back to the internal API category.

How to diagnose it

  • Preserve the occurrence and sanitized route/stage, then inspect original execution evidence before resubmitting state-changing work.

How to fix it

  • No direct repair is available for this occurrence. Use the supported investigation or alternative workflow below.
  • Use the occurrence ID and time to find the traceback in the Server log, or the Gateway log entry 'Gateway agent execution failed.' / 'Gateway agent streaming execution failed.' for command routes. Establish from the task receipt or resource state whether the original operation took effect before any replay, then report the defect with the sanitized context.

Retry and execution caution

  • The outcome cannot establish safe replay. Inspect current state and preserve the occurrence ID before another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The actual defect is diagnosed and original operation state is reconciled.

What not to do

  • Do not delete evidence or invent a configuration change for an unexplained internal failure.

Technical notes

  • Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
